Hi Naomi —

Quick heads up: EdgeAssist is adding a subcontractor, CloudBridge Ltd., to our telemetry/metrics pipeline in EU region for on-the-wire aggregation and short-term buffering. This is a behavioral telemetry processor (no long-term customer content storage).

Attached: edgeassist_subprocessors.csv (roster snapshot).

Ask: can you confirm whether this change requires any additional DPA addendum for Redwood customers in EU and whether there are any onshore restrictions we should be aware of? Also flagging that CloudBridge will perform ephemeral de-duplication and enrichment on metric payloads.

High level controls:
- Data at rest encrypted (AES-256)
- TLS 1.2+ in transit
- Data retention on CloudBridge: 7 days (rolling)
- Processing region: eu-central-1 only

If helpful, Mike Chan (CloudBridge) is cc'd for technical detail.

Thanks,
Sophia Li
Head of Partnerships | EdgeAssist Inc.

Thanks for the heads-up, Sophia. A few clarifying questions before we escalate to legal/security: 

1) When you say "no long-term customer content storage", can you confirm whether any PII or raw customer prompt/response data could appear in the telemetry stream (even transiently)?
2) Is CloudBridge able to access any unredacted customer payloads or encryption keys?
3) Will CloudBridge be operating under EdgeAssist's existing DPA clauses (i.e., covered by our current DPA) or will we need an addendum? If the latter, we'll need an ETA.
4) Does CloudBridge have a current SOC 2 Type II report and do they support customer-managed KMS or HSM?

We have a handful of EU customers with strict residency clauses; I want to confirm there are no egress paths to non-EU locations and that retention limits are enforced. Can Mike provide a short note on the exact data elements they will touch and the network egress topology?

I'll loop in Marissa, Jonas (security), and Karthik (legal) to triage.

Best,
Naomi Feldman

Subject: Re: Notification: new subprocessor 'CloudBridge' (details)

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the questions. A few quick clarifications from CloudBridge: 
- Data scope: CloudBridge will only handle aggregated telemetry and operational metrics (counts, latency histograms, anonymized event markers). We will not store user-generated text or raw prompts.
- PII handling: We explicitly filter and redact email/username fields before ingestion. Small, hashed identifiers may be present to support deduplication; these are one-way hashes.
- Keys/access: We will not receive customer-managed encryption keys. All stored blobs are encrypted with CloudBridge-managed keys; however, we support envelope encryption if EdgeAssist/Redwood requires it (customer-managed KMS integration is available for enterprise accounts).
- Architecture: Processing nodes are deployed in eu-central-1 only. Backups/replication are intra-region. No asynchronous replication to non-EU regions.
- Compliance: We have a recent SOC 2 Type II (summary attached) and our compliance portal is at the Drive link Sophia shared.

Attachments: cloudbridge_soc2_summary.pdf

If you need a transient staging run for validation, we can spin up a test tenant in 48 hours.

Best,
Mike Chan
VP, Product | CloudBridge Ltd.

Sophia / Mike — thanks for the quick clarifications and the SOC 2 summary. Based on the info provided, we can proceed with onboarding but require the following before we mark this as approved for customers with EU residency clauses:

1) Full SOC 2 Type II report (not just summary) or a SOC2 bridge letter from CloudBridge.
2) A signed DPA addendum confirming the processing scope/retention (please use DocuSign link in thread).
3) Confirmation in writing that no customer-managed keys are ingested by CloudBridge (you noted envelope support — please confirm whether EdgeAssist intends to enable that for our customers or not).
4) A short staging test (30–90 minutes) so our ops team can validate that no raw prompt text is present in the telemetry payloads. Mike — can you provision a test tenant and tenant-specific endpoint? Naomi and Marissa will coordinate timing.

If all items are provided, legal will mark the subprocessor roster update as accepted and we will notify affected customers via our standard DPA roster bulletin. If any of the above cannot be provided, we will treat CloudBridge as provisional and require a mitigations plan.

I can sign off on the addendum once Karthik confirms the language, but we'd like the SOC 2 and staging evidence before sending the roster update.

Thanks again — please reply with timelines so we can close this by EOD next week.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
